newsitem.title: USA: NAC Re to end two retrocessional programs.
newsitem.headline: NAC Re to end two retrocessional programs.

text.p: NAC Re Corp said it has reached an agreement to terminate, effective January 1, 1997, two retrocessional programs, in recognition of the company's enhanced surplus position and financial capacity.
NAC Re said it expects to receive a total consideration of about $220 million representing claim reserves of about the same amount.
NAC Re said the statutory surplus of its reinsurance subsidiary, NAC Reinsurance Corp was $663.9 million at December 31, 1996 compared to $615.4 million a year ago.
The company, reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $0.75 a share, in line with Wall Street's First Call consensus estimate.
NAC Re said fourth quarter worldwide net premiums written were $159.3 million, up 14.8 percent. Domestic fourth quarter net premiums written rose 15.8 percent compared to a year ago.
Net premium growth across all the profit centers was favorably impacted by reduced ceded premium charges during the 1996 year, NAC Re said.
This reduction in ceded premiums is principally due to a more cost effective retrocessional program and a moderate increase in the company's retention levels, NAC Re said.
NAC Re said casualty net premiums written grew 2.5 percent in the fourth quarter compared to a year ago.
Property net premiums written rose 10.6 percent in the 1996 fourth quarter compared to a year ago, NAC Re said.
The casualty and property growth can be attributed to increased opportunities from existing facultative and treaty Re said.
Net premiums written from NAC Re's specialty lines, which consist of fidelity/surety, aviation and ocean marine business, increased 35.0 percent to $71.9 million for the 1996 full year.
The increase is primarily attributable to a significant new surety treaty, coupled with an increase in the company's ocean marine business, NAC Re said.
"We are pleased to report record results for the 1996 full year, with strong earnings and quality premium growth," said Ronald L. Bornhuetter, chairman and chief executive officer of NAC Re Corp.

"We enter 1997 with confidence and momentum. Although we expect competitive market conditions to continue, we believe our financial strength and established franchise will allow us to harvest new opportunities and deliver profitable growth, taking full advantage of the dislocations in the marketplace," he said.
